questions.title: Bubble Sort Implementation
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void bubble_sort(int arr[], int n)

It must sort the first n elements ascending using bubble sort (repeatedly swap adjacent out-of-order pairs). The harness prints the sorted array.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the n sorted values, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Selection Sort Implementation
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void selection_sort(int arr[], int n)

It must sort the first n elements ascending using selection sort (select the minimum of the unsorted suffix and swap it into place). The harness prints the sorted array.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the n sorted values, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void insertion_sort(int arr[], int n)

It must sort the first n elements ascending using insertion sort (grow a sorted prefix one element at a time). The harness prints the sorted array.

Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the n sorted values, space-separated.

1 <= n <= 2000, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Bubble Sort Swap Count
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int bubble_swaps(int arr[], int n)

Run bubble sort on a copy of the data and return exactly how many adjacent swaps it performs (this equals the number of inversions). You may sort arr in place while counting.

Input Format:
Line 1: n (n <= 2000). Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the swap count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Insertion Sort Shift Count
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int insertion_shifts(int arr[], int n)

Run insertion sort on the data and return exactly how many element shifts it performs (each time an element moves one slot right). You may sort arr in place while counting.

Input Format:
Line 1: n (n <= 2000). Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the shift count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Ascending Order Check
questions.description:
Sorting is skipped entirely when data is already ordered — the best case. Verify it.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int is_ascending(int arr[], int n)

It must return 1 when arr[0] <= arr[1] <= ... <= arr[n-1], else 0.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Canteen Token Line: One Bubble Pass
questions.description:
The canteen re-orders its token queue with bubble sort, but the bell rings after ONE left-to-right pass (every adjacent pair compared once, swapped when out of order).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void bubble_pass(int arr[], int n)

It must perform exactly one full bubble pass (indices 0..n-2) on the n >= 2 tokens. The harness prints the queue afterwards.

Input Format:
Line 1: n (n >= 2). Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the n values after the pass, space-separated.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 2000, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Race Bibs: Select the Fastest
questions.description:
The race marshal pins the fastest bib first using one selection step: find the smallest number in the whole line and swap it to the front.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void select_min_front(int arr[], int n)

It must swap the minimum element of arr[0..n-1] (first occurrence on ties) with arr[0]. The harness prints the line afterwards.

Input Format:
Line 1: n (n >= 2). Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the n values after the swap, space-separated.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 2000, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Scoreboard Descent Check
questions.description:
A leaderboard is stored best-first, so scores must be non-increasing. Verify the board before publishing.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int is_descending(int arr[], int n)

It must return 1 when arr[0] >= arr[1] >= ... >= arr[n-1], else 0.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Insert the New Runner Card
questions.description:
A coach keeps finished runner cards sorted and slides each new card (the last one in the sheet) into its correct place — one insertion step.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void insert_last(int arr[], int n)

The first n - 1 elements are already ascending; it must insert arr[n-1] where it belongs so all n are ascending. The harness prints the sheet.

Input Format:
Line 1: n (n >= 2). Line 2: n space-separated integers (first n-1 ascending).

Output Format:
One line with the n sorted values, space-separated.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 2000, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Bubble State After K Passes
questions.description:
A teacher traces bubble sort on the class score line. Each pass compares every adjacent pair left to right (indices 0..n-2) and swaps out-of-order pairs. Report the line after exactly k passes.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void bubble_k_passes(int arr[], int n, int k)

It must apply k full passes to the n values in place. The harness prints the resulting line.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: k (0 <= k <= n - 1).

Output Format:
One line with the n values after k passes, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 0 <= k <= n - 1, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Insertion Prefix Sort
questions.description:
An insertion-sort tracer has only processed the first k + 1 elements: the prefix arr[0..k] must be sorted while the tail stays untouched.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void insertion_prefix(int arr[], int n, int k)

It must insertion-sort exactly the prefix of length k + 1 (inserting arr[1]..arr[k] into the growing prefix); elements beyond index k must not move. The harness prints the whole array.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: k (0 <= k <= n - 1).

Output Format:
One line with the n values, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 0 <= k <= n - 1, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Selection Swap Count
questions.description:
The equipment room counts how many physical swaps selection sort performs while ordering bibs: for each position, select the minimum of the unsorted suffix (first occurrence on ties) and swap it into place only when it is not already there.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int selection_swaps(int arr[], int n)

It must return the number of swaps selection sort performs (you may sort arr in place while counting).

Input Format:
Line 1: n (n <= 2000). Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the swap count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Sort Cards by Digit Sum
questions.description:
A numerology game orders cards by the sum of their digits, ascending. Equal digit sums keep their original relative order, so the sort must be stable — insertion sort with a digit-sum comparison.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void sort_by_digit_sum(int arr[], int n)

It must sort the n values in place by digit sum (stable). The harness prints the ordered cards.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated non-negative integers.

Output Format:
One line with the n ordered values, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= value <= 1000000000

questions.title: Selection Pass Trace
questions.description:
A sorting tracer runs selection sort one pass at a time. Pass number s (0-based) selects the minimum of arr[s..n-1] (first occurrence on ties) and swaps it into position s. The harness applies passes s = 0 .. k-1 and prints the array after each one.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void selection_pass(int arr[], int n, int start)

It must perform exactly ONE selection pass starting at index start.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: k (1 <= k <= n - 1).

Output Format:
k lines, each with the n values after that pass, space-separated.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 30, 1 <= k <= n - 1, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Comparison Count Report
questions.description:
A lab compares two sorters on the same data: bubble sort WITH an early exit (stop when a full pass makes no swap) and selection sort. The report shows how many element comparisons each performs on the given input.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void comparison_report(int arr[], int n, int *bubble, int *selection)

It must store the bubble comparison count into *bubble and the selection comparison count into *selection (selection always compares exactly n * (n - 1) / 2). The harness prints both.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the bubble count, then the selection count, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Cocktail Shaker Sort
questions.description:
A drinks plant orders crates with cocktail shaker sort: a left-to-right bubble pass, then a right-to-left pass, alternating until a full pass swaps nothing.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void cocktail_sort(int arr[], int n)

It must sort the n values ascending in place. The harness prints the sorted crates.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the n sorted values, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Sort by Frequency Then Value
questions.description:
A streaming service ranks watch counts: values sort by DESCENDING frequency; equal frequencies sort by ascending value.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void frequency_sort(int arr[], int n)

All values are in 0..100. It must rearrange arr in place accordingly. The harness prints the result.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers (each 0..100).

Output Format:
One line with the n rearranged values, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= value <= 100

questions.title: Dutch Flag Weights
questions.description:
A recycling plant sorts crates marked 0, 1 or 2 (light, medium, heavy) in a SINGLE pass with three moving pointers and no counting array — the Dutch flag partition.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void sort_three_weights(int arr[], int n)

Every value is 0, 1 or 2. It must rearrange arr ascending in place using the three-way partition. The harness prints the result.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers (each 0, 1 or 2).

Output Format:
One line with the n sorted values, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, value is 0, 1 or 2

questions.title: Pancake Sort by Flips
questions.description:
A short-order cook sorts pancake stacks with a spatula: the only move is reversing a prefix. Pancake sort finds the largest remaining pancake, flips it to the top, then flips it down to its final position.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void pancake_sort(int arr[], int n)

It must sort the n values ascending in place using prefix reversals only. The harness prints the sorted stack.

Input Format:
Line 1: n (n <= 50). Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the n sorted values, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, |value| <= 1000000000
